title: RAG status reporting
metaDescription: RAG status reporting where each red, amber, or green is earned from the work, not chosen by the reporter. Husn reads Jira, Slack, and docs and shows the reason behind every color.
heroHeadline: Red, amber, green you can trace.
heroSubheadline: A RAG report is only worth reading if the colors mean something. Husn assigns each one from the work itself and attaches the reason, so a green is a fact rather than a hope.
primaryPain: In most RAG reports the color says more about the person filling it in than about the project. An optimist marks amber green, a worrier marks green amber, and neither can point to the work that justifies the choice. By the time a color is wrong enough to matter, the cost of being wrong has already landed.
painBullets: The color is a judgment call, so the same project can be red on one desk and green on another.
Nothing concrete sits behind the rating, so it cannot be questioned in a review or trusted in a roll up.
Colors are set on a schedule, so a project goes amber in the work days before the report agrees.
whyHardHeading: Why RAG breaks down at scale
whyHard: Roll a hundred hand picked colors up into a portfolio view and the aggregate inherits every soft call underneath it.
A green with no reason cannot be defended when a stakeholder pushes, so the report loses authority the moment it is challenged.
Keeping every color honest by hand each cycle is more work than anyone has time for, so the easy answer wins and the report drifts.
howHusnHelps: Husn sets each color from live signals across Jira, Slack, and docs, so the rating reflects where the work actually stands.
Every color carries the reason that earned it, the slipped date, the aging blocker, the scope that grew unremarked, so the rating holds up under questioning.
Husn watches the signals between cycles and moves a color early, so a project shows amber while there is still a cheap fix, not after the incident.
